description: Customer support ticket routing, 27 fine-grained intents
hf_source: bitext/Bitext-customer-support-llm-chatbot-training-dataset (intent column, not category), augmented: see scripts/build_support_ticket_v3.py

label_descriptions.cancel_order: Stop an order from happening. Not a refund request: no money has been asked for yet. Compare get_refund, check_cancellation_fee
label_descriptions.change_order: Modify the contents of an order already placed, such as items or quantity. Compare change_shipping_address for the destination
label_descriptions.change_shipping_address: Change the delivery address on an existing order. Note: rows do not cover packages already in transit, so in-transit redirects have no correct class here
label_descriptions.check_cancellation_fee: Ask what cancelling would cost, without yet cancelling. Compare cancel_order, which acts
label_descriptions.check_invoice: Look at or query an invoice that already exists. Compare get_invoice, which asks to be sent one
label_descriptions.check_payment_methods: Ask which payment methods are accepted. Compare payment_issue, where a payment has failed
label_descriptions.check_refund_policy: Ask what the refund rules are. Compare get_refund, which asks for money back under them
label_descriptions.complaint: Express dissatisfaction without a specific actionable request. Acts as a catch-all sink: unrelated input often lands here with moderate confidence, so this class needs its own rule rather than a confidence gate
label_descriptions.contact_customer_service: Ask how to reach support, by any channel
label_descriptions.contact_human_agent: Ask specifically for a person rather than automation. Compare contact_customer_service, which is channel-agnostic
label_descriptions.create_account: Open a new account. Compare registration_problems, where creating one failed
label_descriptions.delete_account: Close or remove an account permanently
label_descriptions.delivery_options: Ask which shipping methods or speeds are available, before choosing. Compare delivery_period, which asks how long
label_descriptions.delivery_period: Ask how long delivery takes in general. Compare track_order, which asks where one specific shipment is now
label_descriptions.edit_account: Change details on an existing account, such as name or email
label_descriptions.get_invoice: Ask to be sent or issued an invoice. Compare check_invoice, which queries one that exists
label_descriptions.get_refund: Ask for money back when none has been promised yet. Compare track_refund, where a refund is already expected
label_descriptions.newsletter_subscription: Subscribe to or unsubscribe from the newsletter
label_descriptions.payment_issue: A payment failed, was declined, or was charged wrongly. Compare check_payment_methods, which only asks what is accepted
label_descriptions.place_order: Buy something, or ask how to. Thin vocabulary coverage: 'I want to place a new order' misroutes, so treat low confidence here as unresolved rather than as this class
label_descriptions.recover_password: Reset or recover a forgotten password. Compare registration_problems, which is about signing up
label_descriptions.registration_problems: Signing up failed or is blocked. Compare create_account, which is the plain request
label_descriptions.review: Leave, change or ask about a product or service review
label_descriptions.set_up_shipping_address: Add a shipping address for the first time. Compare change_shipping_address, which replaces an existing one
label_descriptions.switch_account: Move between accounts the customer already has. Lowest coverage class at a 0.9 gate (0.44), so a global high threshold discards most correct answers here
label_descriptions.track_order: Ask where one specific shipment is now. Trained on parcel, package and shipment as well as order, since v2 keyed on the noun and missed every phrasing that avoided the word 'order'
label_descriptions.track_refund: A refund is already expected and the customer asks where it is. Compare get_refund, which asks for one in the first place
